name: Major cyber incidents
value: France blamed IRGC unit 9 Nov; nothing new
summary: France's 9 Nov attribution of store fridge sabotage to an IRGC unit is a week old; no new national-scale attack found
state: On 9–10 Nov France attributed the October sabotage of refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail sites to Shahid Kaveh, a unit tied to Iran's Revolutionary Guards, and summoned Iran's ambassador (The Record; Khaleej Times). Iran rejected the accusation. Searches to 16 Nov found no new national-scale attack on critical infrastructure, and the attribution is now a week old, so the level moves down to Watch.
for_you: Follow NCSC guidance on updating devices and watching for phishing; businesses with connected building systems should check vendor advisories.
rubric_hit: Recent state-attributed attack on retail systems, no new national attack = Watch

why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.
drivers: Ransomware gangs, state actors, zero-days, supply-chain compromises.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.
